summary: Inference-time optimization is often where the biggest cost savings live, since the same product request can cost 10-100x more depending on model choice, prompt length, and caching strategy. Most teams can cut LLM spend by 50-80% without any quality loss by combining prompt caching, model routing, and response caching. Latency improvements of 2-10x are also commonly achievable through streaming, smaller models, and semantic caching.

techniques.name: Prompt (Context) Caching
techniques.description: Reuse cached static portions of prompts (system instructions, few-shot examples, large documents) so the provider doesn't re-process identical prefix tokens on every call.
techniques.savings: 50-90% reduction on input tokens for the cached prefix
techniques.example: With Anthropic, add a cache_control breakpoint to your large system prompt/document so repeated queries against the same context only pay ~10% of the input token cost after the first call.

techniques.name: Model Routing / Right-Sizing
techniques.description: Route simple requests to cheap, fast models (e.g. GPT-4o-mini, Claude Haiku, Gemini Flash) and reserve expensive frontier models only for hard tasks, optionally using a cheap classifier to decide.
techniques.savings: 60-90% reduction vs. always using a flagship model
techniques.example: Use a tiny model to classify intent, then send FAQ-style queries to Haiku and only escalate ambiguous reasoning tasks to Claude Sonnet/GPT-4o.

techniques.name: Exact-Match Response Caching
techniques.description: Store full responses keyed by a hash of the exact prompt/params and return instantly for repeat identical requests, skipping the LLM entirely.
techniques.example: Hash {model, temperature, prompt} into a Redis key with a TTL and short-circuit the API call when the key exists.

techniques.name: Semantic Caching
techniques.description: Embed incoming queries and return a cached answer when a new query is semantically similar (above a cosine threshold) to a previous one, even if not worded identically.
techniques.example: Use GPTCache or Redis vector search so 'how do I reset my password' and 'reset password steps' both hit the same cached answer.

techniques.name: Prompt Compression / Trimming
techniques.description: Remove redundant instructions, compress context with tools like LLMLingua, and drop unneeded few-shot examples or chat history to shrink input tokens.
techniques.example: Run long retrieved documents through LLMLingua to compress them 3-5x before injecting into the prompt while preserving answer quality.

techniques.name: Output Token Limiting & Structured Output
techniques.description: Cap max_tokens, request concise or JSON-only responses, and use structured output modes to avoid verbose, expensive generations.
techniques.savings: 20-50% reduction on output tokens (the most expensive tokens)
techniques.example: Set max_tokens=150 and instruct 'Respond only with the JSON object, no prose' to stop the model padding answers.

techniques.name: Retrieval-Augmented Context Reduction (RAG)
techniques.description: Instead of stuffing entire knowledge bases into the prompt, retrieve only the top-k relevant chunks, drastically cutting input tokens per call.
techniques.example: Use a vector DB to fetch the 3 most relevant doc chunks for a question rather than pasting a 50-page manual into every request.

techniques.name: Batching Requests
techniques.description: Group many independent requests into a batch API that runs asynchronously at a discounted rate, ideal for non-realtime workloads.
techniques.example: Submit 10,000 document summaries via OpenAI's Batch API overnight for 50% off standard token pricing.

techniques.name: Streaming Responses
techniques.description: Stream tokens as they generate to improve perceived latency and allow early termination once enough output is produced.
techniques.savings: 0-20% token savings via early stopping; large perceived latency win
techniques.example: Stream the response and stop generation client-side once a complete JSON object is detected, avoiding trailing filler tokens.

techniques.name: Fallback & Retry Optimization
techniques.description: Use exponential backoff, provider fallbacks, and avoid blind retries that double-charge; cache partial results to prevent redoing expensive work on failure.
techniques.savings: 10-30% reduction by eliminating wasted duplicate calls
techniques.example: Configure LiteLLM to retry on a cheaper secondary model with backoff instead of hammering the primary endpoint and paying for failed calls.

techniques.name: Quantized / Self-Hosted Open Models
techniques.description: Serve open-weight models (Llama, Qwen, Mistral) with quantization (GPTQ/AWQ/GGUF) on your own GPUs for high-volume predictable workloads.
techniques.savings: 70-95% reduction at scale vs. per-token API pricing
techniques.example: Deploy a 4-bit quantized Llama 3.1 8B on vLLM to handle classification traffic that would otherwise cost thousands/month in API fees.

tools.name: GPTCache
tools.description: Open-source semantic caching layer that stores and retrieves LLM responses by embedding similarity to avoid redundant calls.

tools.name: LiteLLM
tools.description: Unified proxy/SDK for 100+ LLM providers with built-in caching, routing, fallbacks, rate limiting, and cost tracking.
tools.pricing_paid: Open source free; Enterprise plans from ~$250/mo for SSO, admin UI, and support

tools.name: Helicone
tools.description: LLM observability and gateway platform offering request logging, caching, cost analytics, and rate limiting via a proxy.
tools.pricing_paid: Free tier (10k requests/mo); Pro from $20/user/mo, with scaling usage-based pricing

tools.name: Redis (Semantic Cache)
tools.description: In-memory data store with vector search used for both exact-match and semantic LLM response caching at low latency.
tools.pricing_paid: Open source free; Redis Cloud from ~$5/mo, enterprise/Flex plans usage-based

tools.name: LangChain
tools.description: Framework for building LLM apps with built-in caching (InMemory, Redis, SQLite), prompt management, and routing abstractions.
tools.pricing_paid: Open source free; LangSmith observability from $39/user/mo

tools.name: LLMLingua
tools.description: Microsoft's prompt compression library that shrinks prompts up to 20x while preserving key information to reduce input tokens.

tools.name: Portkey
tools.description: AI gateway offering caching (simple + semantic), load balancing, fallbacks, observability, and guardrails across providers.
tools.pricing_paid: Free tier (10k requests/mo); Production plans from ~$49/mo plus usage

tools.name: vLLM
tools.description: High-throughput open-source inference engine with PagedAttention and continuous batching for efficiently self-hosting open models.
tools.pricing_paid: Free and open source (you pay for your own compute)

quick_wins: Enable provider prompt caching for your large static system prompts and documents (near-zero code change, 50-90% savings on repeated prefixes).
Add exact-match response caching with Redis keyed on prompt+params to eliminate duplicate calls instantly.
Route simple/short queries to a cheap model (GPT-4o-mini, Claude Haiku, Gemini Flash) and only escalate hard tasks to flagship models.
Set a sensible max_tokens and ask for concise/JSON-only output to cut the expensive output token bill.
Move non-realtime bulk jobs (summaries, classification, backfills) to the provider's Batch API for roughly 50% off.
